senses.gloss: f. (פרר or נפר √פר) a break, division, whence
the purchase of an odd object, of one of a pair.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 80b:5">Sabb. 80ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="A02114"><he>אַנְדִּיפָא</he></cite> q. v.) <he>וכי אדם עושה מעותיו א׳</he> will a man buy a half of a thing (as a cosmetic for one temple)?

senses.gloss: partial payments, an agreement (invalid according to Jewish law) of term payments with the condition of forfeiture on missing one term (v. אַסְמַכְתָּא), esp. such an agreement forced upon a Jew by a gentile (Roman) individual or authority.
units: Gitt. 44ᵃ (v. אָנַס) אם בא׳ if his crop was seized in consequence of an anparuth, he is exempt from paying the tithes (of his produces, since he is the loser, whereas if distrained for a real debt, he enjoys the legal benefit of being released of a debt, and therefore must pay the tithes, as if he had sold the crop). Y. Keth. X, end, 34ᵃ בארנונה וכ׳ with reference to annona, capitation tax and forfeiture.

<cite ref="Gittin 58b:7">Gitt. 58ᵇ</cite> <he>הבא מחמת חוב ומחמת א׳ וכ׳</he> if a gentile (Roman) obtained possession of a Jew’s property in consequence of seizure for a debt or of forfeiture and subsequently sold it to a Jew, the Sicarion law finds no application (and the property must, without any indemnity, be restored to its original owner; v. <cite ref="O00825"><he>סִיקְרִיקוֹן</he></cite>); <he>וא׳ עצמה וכ׳</he> and the property seized for forfeiture must have been in the possession of the gentile for twelve months (during which the Jew might have had a chance to reclaim it as illegally seized; v., however, the objection, and subsequent emendation of <he>סיקריקין</he> for <he>א׳</he>, ibid.).

Ib. אין א׳ בבבל in Babylon (under the Persian government) there is no anparuth, (which is interpreted) אין דין א׳ וכ׳ the laws concerning the purchase by a Jew of property which a gentile had seized for forfeiture find no application in the well regulated Persian state because the owner might have gone to court, if he felt himself aggrieved.

<cite ref="Tosefta Gittin 5:2">Tosef. Gitt. V</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Gittin 3:2">III</cite>), 2.—Pl. <he>אַנְפָּרִיּוֹת</he>. Y’lamd. Sh’laḥ. (quot. in Ar.) <he>אני נוטל מהן א׳ וכ׳</he> I (the Lord) take from them promises to pay in instalments (promises of amending their ways, repentance) and give them extension. Tanḥ.
ib., end, a citizen was paying annonæ וכותב א׳ and signing agreements of forfeiture; (Num. R. s. 17 אפכיות, v. אַפּוּכִי). [Ibid. s. 2 אנפריאות, v. אַנְפּוֹרָא pl.]
